analysis_notes.download: 576x1024 h264 30 fps, 41.9 MB (lowest format TikTok offers is 540p-class; no <=480p rendition exists). Kept on Spark (<300 MB). TikTok download variant carries a TikTok/@mraevq watermark that is not part of the original composition.
analysis_notes.transcript_source: TikTok auto-captions eng-US (482 cues, 3326 words); full text in research/library/transcripts/7664930759395888416.txt. Names are mis-transcribed in places (Chenji/Chen Jie, Wang Chung/Wang Qiang, Lin Fung/Lin Feng, Chen Dashing/Chen Dashan); the burned-in subtitles spell them Chen Jie, Wang Qiang, Lili, Chen Dashan, Lin Feng.

analysis_notes.metadata_snapshot: yt-dlp 2026-11-01 ~09:06 UTC. Follower count not exposed by the TikTok extractor (subs null). Audio track labelled 'original sound' (原創音樂).
analysis_notes.originality_warning: Translated repost of a Chinese 2D animated web-series (rule-horror / 规则怪谈 genre). Study structure and devices only; do not reuse plot (rule entities, cleaners, Zone Zero, anchor), characters or lines.

title_pattern.notes: No descriptive title at all: the caption is two character-name hashtags, i.e. the account treats each upload as an episode of a recurring cast (series SEO / searchable names), and lets the cover frame plus the first 5 s do all the selling. On TikTok the title is barely visible, so this is not a pattern to copy for YouTube; for TikTok it signals 'this is part of a series you can binge'. For our use: keep a recurring named cast and tag them, but add a curiosity line for YouTube Shorts / long-form.

thumbnail.composition: TikTok cover = the opening frame. 9:16 canvas that is ~60% black: a rounded ~4:3 story panel sits in the vertical middle. Inside it, a split interior: left half a doorway with the son (yellow-green jacket, pale face, worried brow) being pulled by the wrist; right half the father (black T-shirt, tan trousers) mid-stride toward the exit, looking back with wide white-ringed 'terror eyes'. Hands joined at the centre line.
thumbnail.text: None (no title card on the cover; only the TikTok watermark in this download).
thumbnail.colours: Desaturated greys and blue floor; the only saturated element is the son's neon yellow-green jacket. Black letterbox all around.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Two full-body characters at equal scale; contrast is emotional rather than scale: calm-worried son vs. panicked father, joined hands = 'being dragged away'. The father's tiny pupils in big white eye rings are the focal point.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Reads instantly as 'someone is fleeing from something' with zero text; the panic face is the hook. The neon jacket makes the protagonist recognisable across a whole series of covers. Cheap, consistent cutout-cartoon style signals 'animated story series' in the feed. Weak as a YouTube thumbnail (no text, tiny subject on black), fine as a TikTok cover where the video autoplays.

hook.verbatim_0_to_5s: Late one night, Dad dragged me outside. "Run! It's coming!" "Don't look back." He drove us to another city.
hook.verbatim_5_to_11s: The next day, I checked the news. Everyone in our complex died in their sleep. Two families survived because they were away.
hook.device: In-medias-res night flight in first person, with an unnamed threat ('It') and a rule planted in the first 3 seconds ('Don't look back'), then a mass-casualty payoff at 7 s that proves the threat is real and makes the dad a suspect (he knew). Every line is <2 s, one action per line, no setup or intro. The planted rule is paid off in the final dialogue line of the climax (13:43 'Don't look back').

beats.summary: Night flight: dad drags narrator out, 'it's coming', 'don't look back', drives to another city.
News: whole apartment complex died in their sleep; only two families (theirs + one other) were away.
Son accuses dad of knowing; dad refuses: 'being alive is enough', 'it's beyond description'.
Phone rings, caller ID terrifies dad, 'They found us', must leave; refuses to explain ('some things are safer left unknown').
Spycraft: new phone + SIM, smashes old phone, memorise a number then eat the note, 'if we get separated, call it'.

Drive (dad never checks the mirror), backpacks with shovel, forest walk; dad reveals college research into unknown phenomena, ancient rules, shut-down project, secrecy agreements, 'once known a rule never lets you go'.

Bare cabin safe house: 'we're marked like a candle in the dark'; the don't-look-back rule (noticing it marks you, it erases you and everyone nearby); warning-system alert; the elderly couple across the hall also survived.
Knocking at night: voice of 'Uncle Li' from across the hall, with a true personal detail (rice dumplings); son moves to open, dad stops him: 'You're the fake one!'

Dawn: the thing copied memory and voice; dad admits there are many rules/'rule entities' from an ancient journal; Professor Chen's 7-person group, 3 vanished with the lab; quest set: find technician Lin Feng who found a place that blocks the rules.
Eye-in-a-circle symbol carved on a tree ('it's marking its prey'); dad sees a shadow move: 'It's following us! Run!'
While running: Lin Feng secretly kept the data, calls entities 'cosmic viruses', copying has limits (computer clogged with junk); destination = abandoned weather station in the NW wasteland.
Deserted road, son wants to flag a car, dad yanks him into the weeds; the black SUV bears the same eye symbol; it idles 10 minutes, watching, then leaves.
'Cleaners': humans who erase triggers, marked people and witnesses; 'worse because they're human'; 'prey between two monsters'.
Mountains at dusk, exhaustion, bread, abandoned railway; dad relays Prof. Chen's 'immune system' theory (we are the virus).
Stone cairn + empty can by the tracks: someone was here recently. Friend or enemy?

Tunnel at night: flashlight reveals countless bat-like monsters hanging overhead, two shriek and drop, chase, battery dies, dad falls ('leave me, run'), scream behind; then dad reappears wounded (fake-out death).
Abandoned train cars and a camp with a dead campfire and stone stove; someone has lived here.

Armed man with rifle + young woman + scholarly man; cover story fails ('travelers carrying a military shovel'); admitting they came through the tunnel stuns them; 'we're all fleeing things that shouldn't exist'; rifle lowered, wounds treated.

Introductions (Uncle Ma, Wang Qiang, daughter Lili); their rule = a sound from village loudspeakers at night; anyone who heard it vanished; cotton in ears, cellar for 3 days; village empty; helicopters + fire = cleaners.
Wang Qiang's map: NW wasteland has weak magnetic signal; dad: 'the weather station?'; join forces; Uncle Ma's terms (my orders, my daughter's safety).
Marching order; burnt crater from an incendiary bomb (cleaners were here); abandoned cleaner vehicle with an advanced radio-like device, battery dead.
Cave at dusk, '10 more days'; a drone hovers at the cave mouth then leaves: 'they're only marking us... like a cat playing with mice'; no one sleeps.
Canyon with one wooden bridge; halfway across, cleaners in red hazmat suits appear behind, then ahead: planned trap.
Lead cleaner: 'Target locked. Chen Dashan, sole Chimera survivor. Execute final cleanup protocol.' Dad shows no surprise; he always knew.

Blue-tipped weapons fire, dad's eyes glow the same blue, he deflects the beams ('he's not breaking down, he's awakening'); 'Jump! Find Lin Feng'; dad turns transparent, smiles, says the planted rule 'Don't look back.'; they jump.
Sandy shore; Uncle Ma missing; Lili cries then recovers; a day later they reach the weather station: empty, dusty for decades.

Lin Feng's journal: rule entities are the world's source code, self-aware life is the bug, cleaners are the repair program; Zone Zero is a blank zone outside the system that needs an anchor: 'Chen Dashan is that anchor.'
'Dad had never been fleeing. Every step led toward his destiny.' He became the anchor; his sacrifice left one final refuge. 'The end.'

pacing.narration_density: Continuous narration from 0.18 s to 15:16; almost no pauses, no music-only breaks. Lines average ~1.9 s (482 caption cues). First-person narrator voice reads both narration and the quoted dialogue.
pacing.shot_rhythm: Visual change every ~2-3 s throughout (14-27 per minute), usually a reframe of the same 2D scene matched to each subtitle line; action moments compress to 4-5 cuts per second (phone smash 0:48). One deliberate exception: the 42 s static journal insert for the final reveal, where the words carry everything.
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: New threat, reveal or set piece every ~30-60 s: 0:07 mass death, 0:22 phone call, 2:28 knocking imposter, 4:04 eye symbol, 5:04 cleaner car, 7:12 tunnel monsters, 8:16 rifle standoff, 12:00 drone, 12:34 trap, 13:15 transformation, 14:24 journal truth.
pacing.structure_timing_pct: Hook 0-1%; inciting proof by 1%; quest objective set at 26% (3:56); second antagonist at 33%; midpoint ally group at 54%; trap/climax 82-90%; final reveal 94-99%.

techniques_worth_copying: Plant a one-line rule in the first 3 s ('Don't look back') and make it the last spoken line of the climax: a closed loop that rewards watching 15 minutes.
Hook = first-person in medias res + unnamed threat ('It') + proof via casualty count within 8 s; no intro, no title card.
Withheld-answer dialogue: the parent knows and refuses ('some things are safer left unknown'), releasing lore in 3-4 scheduled drops spaced through the walk.
Rule-horror logic: each rule = trigger + consequence + countermeasure (look back -> marked; hear the sound -> vanish; cotton in ears + cellar). Easy to invent original rules in the same shape.
Escalating two-front threat: supernatural entity plus a human 'cleaner' faction that is 'worse because they're human'; recurring visual sigil (eye-in-circle) ties both and becomes the series' mark.
Travel-quest skeleton: named destination + named mentor (Lin Feng, weather station) set at ~25%, then location-of-the-week set pieces (cabin, road, tunnel, train camp, cave, bridge) every ~60 s.
Concrete, homely detail sells the imposter scare (egg yolk rice dumplings two days ago).
Fake-out death (dad falls in tunnel, scream, reappears wounded) mid-video, then a real sacrifice at the climax.
Twist via antagonist reading the hero's file aloud ('Target locked. <full name>, sole <project> survivor').
Final reveal through a found document read verbatim over a single held insert; reframes the whole journey ('he had never been fleeing').
One shot per subtitle line: cheap reframes of the same puppet set keep visual change ~every 2.9 s.
Sound-effect graphics instead of animation: yellow/red zigzag lines for ringing, screaming, noise; starburst for knocks.
Neon-jacket protagonist = instant recognition across thumbnails and an episodic cast tagged by name in the caption.

code_only_remake_needs.format: 1080x1920 canvas, black background, centred rounded-corner ~4:3 story panel (~1040x760, radius ~24 px) in the middle third; subtitle line inside the panel bottom. Leaves top/bottom black for the platform UI. Easy in Remotion.
code_only_remake_needs.characters: Flat cutout puppets in SVG: big-head chibi proportions (head ~1/3 of height), pale or tan skin, black hair shapes, flat clothing fills with simple shading; swappable eye sets (normal, narrowed, white-ring terror eyes with tiny pupils, glowing cyan) and brows/mouths for expressions; jointed arms for point/pull/raise/hand-to-face; 2-3 frame walk/run cycle with body bob. Need ~5 characters with one signature colour each (neon jacket, black tee, pink cardigan, red hair, denim).
code_only_remake_needs.backgrounds: ~20 flat SVG sets with muted palettes: living room with window, phone store, car interior/exterior, forest (dark green layered bushes), cabin interior (amber), dark doorway, deserted road, rail tracks, tunnel (near black + light cone mask), train carriage, village rooftop with loudspeaker, cave/sunset (orange gradient), canyon bridge, beach, dusty station interior. Parallax layers for walking/running.
code_only_remake_needs.inserts_and_props: Phone with article text, paper note, backpack contents, ancient journal page (procedural handwritten glyph rows on parchment), eye-in-circle sigil, black SUV, radio device, drone, hazmat figures, weapons with glowing tips, claw-scratch wound, campfire, stone cairn.
code_only_remake_needs.camera: Virtual camera per shot: hard cut between reframes of the same scene on every subtitle line, slow 2-5% push-in during holds, punch-in to inserts, occasional slow pan; screen shake for impacts; fast 4-5 cut action bursts.
code_only_remake_needs.fx: SVG zigzag 'sound' strokes (ringing, scream, noise) flickering at 6-8 fps; starburst impact; glow (feGaussianBlur) for cyan eyes/weapons and beams; opacity fade for the sacrifice; colour-tint overlays (green for hiding, red for the imposter, orange sky for climax); smoke loops; flashlight cone via radial mask.
code_only_remake_needs.audio_text: Original first-person script ~3,300 words for 15 min (~217 wpm; Kokoro TTS at speed ~1.15-1.25), one subtitle line per TTS sentence with word timings driving cut points; light ambient drone + stingers on reveals. Captions small white sans with soft shadow (not karaoke style).
code_only_remake_needs.pipeline: Storyboard JSON: list of shots {bg, characters with pose/expression/position, insert, camera move, fx, line}. Because shots are ~1 per line, the storyboard can be generated from the script automatically with a scene/location state machine; the key manual art cost is the puppet rig + ~20 backgrounds, then reuse across episodes.
